# Independent audit of the zero-slack centroid-graph obstruction



The minimum of the three affine height functions gives the stated actual convex polytope and all eight full-dimensional integer fibers. Replacing it by the hull of those fibers preserves their exact identities and adds no integer base. The tabulated parity maxima are unique for every \(R\ge0,d\ge1\). All four midpoint edges have exact base and radius equalities, hence exact Minkowski set equality.

The centroid graph is affinely isomorphic to the displayed three-dimensional graph. Each of the five selected points is strictly exposed in its hull; the three exclusion inequalities remove all omitted graph points. Its five deletion hulls therefore give a direct Helly witness, without any inference from affine rank. The additional integer-base representation has height nine rather than sixteen, demonstrating explicitly why the forest relations do not imply full Jensen affinity.

The \(d=2,R=1\) area normalization is correct. The two midpoint pairs at \(G_4\) are disjoint and exclude the center itself, so a containing closed halfspace must contain three distinct centroids with the claimed minimum total fiber weight. Grünbaum then proves the stated strict OC lower bound for this instance. The graph-Helly obstruction is correctly separated from any OC counterexample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
